readme: Evidence file for ECX2320 Stage 1. Every figure carries a source, a URL and an access date. Entries with verified:false are GAPS, not estimates: nothing has been guessed or filled in to make a table look complete. scripts/calculations.mjs reads this file and refuses to compute any calculation whose inputs are unverified.
accessedBy: Read directly from each company's own live website using a browser, not from a coupon or comparison site.

competitors.name: My Muscle Chef
competitors.positioning: Mass market high protein ready meals
competitors.priceNotes: Homepage states 'Over 70+ ready made meals from $10.95'. Individual tiles observed at $10.95, $11.95 and $12.95. A time limited 'Chef's Special' at $7.95 was also running on the access date.
competitors.scale: 4.3 from 3,233 reviews shown on the homepage. Claims '#1 Healthy Ready Meal Brand', sourced on their page to Nielsen data to 09.09.25.
competitors.range: 80+ meals, 100+ items including snacks and drinks
competitors.sampleNote: Seven meals visible on the homepage carousel on the access date. This is a convenience sample of what the company chose to feature, not a random sample of the full menu, and it is likely to flatter them.

competitors.name: Dineamic
competitors.positioning: Premium ready meals, free range and grass fed, carbon neutral
competitors.priceNotes: Page title reads '$11.95 Pre Made Meals'. Ten meal bundles listed at $115.76 reduced from $120.50, which is $11.58 a meal. States no lock in contracts.
competitors.scale: Homepage claims 'OVER 3700+ 5 STAR REVIEWS', plus '4.5-star across 1,200+ reviews' and '4.6-star across 220+ reviews' from two named platforms.
competitors.range: Bundles for High Protein, Calorie Smart, Low FODMAP and Mediterranean Diet
competitors.sampleNote: Four best sellers shown on the homepage with full macros on the access date.

competitors.name: Muscle Meals Direct
competitors.base: Delivers to Melbourne among other cities
competitors.positioning: Explicitly gym and physique focused, the closest competitor to this segment
competitors.priceNotes: Every meal tile on the homepage listed at a regular price of $15.95 on the access date.
competitors.scale: No review count or customer number published on the homepage.
competitors.range: Meals, snacks and protein shakes with a menu builder and an optional subscription
competitors.sampleNote: No macros published on the homepage, so protein and carbohydrate per meal could not be verified. Named meals are carbohydrate forward: sweet potato, protein pasta, brown rice.

competitors.name: Youfoodz
competitors.positioning: Subscription ready meals, owned by HelloFresh
competitors.priceNotes: No per meal price is shown before entering the subscription flow. The homepage offer on the access date was 'Get up to 40% off + free add-ons for 12 weeks, new subscribers only, varies by plan'. Per meal price NOT VERIFIED.
competitors.scale: States over 80 meal options every week.
competitors.range: 80+ meals weekly, including a 'Macro Controlled' line
competitors.sampleNote: Menu is carbohydrate forward. Featured meals include naan and brown rice, chips, bacon loaded mac and cheese, penne, spaghetti and lasagne.

gaps.needed: Number of people in Greater Melbourne who train regularly with strength or physique goals
gaps.whyItMatters: Calculation 1, market sizing. Everything downstream scales off it.
gaps.whereToGetIt: AusPlay participation data by state and activity at clearinghouseforsport.gov.au, filtered to Victoria and to fitness or gym activities. Cross check against ABS Estimated Resident Population for Greater Melbourne.
gaps.doNotDo: Do not estimate this from memory or from an AI answer. The rubric treats invented figures as academic misconduct.

gaps.needed: Share of that population who both track macros and say time is what stops them prepping
gaps.whereToGetIt: Your own intercept survey at a gym, with the instrument and raw responses kept for Appendix C. A published industry report is acceptable if you can cite the page.

gaps.needed: Trays a week your kitchen can actually produce
gaps.whyItMatters: Calculation 5, capacity share, and Calculation 8, cost to serve.
gaps.whereToGetIt: A quoted commercial kitchen hire rate and hours, or a named co packer's stated minimum and maximum run.

gaps.needed: Ingredient, packaging, labour and delivery cost of one tray
gaps.whereToGetIt: Price a single recipe at wholesale, for example Bidfood or a market supplier, plus tray and film cost, plus a costed labour minute rate, plus a courier quote for a Melbourne metro drop.

gaps.needed: A dated change that opened this window
gaps.whyItMatters: Week 2 demand shifters, and the 'why now' section of the analysis.
candidatesToVerify: Growth in GLP-1 medication use in Australia and the protein requirement that comes with rapid weight loss. Verifiable from PBS or TGA publications with a date.
HelloFresh acquisition of Youfoodz and any subsequent range or service change. Verifiable from company announcements with a date.
Change in Melbourne commercial kitchen availability or food delivery costs. Needs a dated source.
gaps.doNotDo: Pick one and verify it with a dated, citable source before it goes in the analysis.

ratio.note: Computed from data/meals.json by scripts/calculations.mjs. Included here so the comparison table has both sides in one place.
